PullRequest.Title: chore: update to Electron 43
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331466
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332131
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327088
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/251777
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319725

Additionally reverts https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ba2a3ee73709588f8e6fa58441208d3b5c0457c7 for system fontconfig initialization issue in favor of the fix in the runtime https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/673915bfe773f3f62219f96bfc787337a6e88203, fyi @alexdima @alexr00

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed workflow ordering, the root npm lifecycle declaration, and the preinstall implementation are all explicit. The cache-miss condition means the `.postinstall-state` guard stored under root `node_modules` cannot suppress the first execution, and root `npm ci` recreates that directory before running its lifecycle, so it cannot suppress the second. Only the exact duration varies with runner caches and network speed.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Nested npm/node-gyp subprocesses, package filesystem operations, and Electron/Node header cache or network I/O.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The duplicate full preinstall occurs once per node_modules cache-miss job and multiplies across the six changed workflow jobs (and any architecture/template expansions); cold header/npm caches make each duplicate more expensive.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased cache-miss build latency and lower CI throughput from duplicated subprocess and I/O work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, these jobs ran only root `npm ci`, which invoked the existing `preinstall` lifecycle once. They did not execute a separate full preinstall beforehand.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: On every node_modules cache miss, the job now executes the full preinstall once explicitly and once again as part of the immediately following root `npm ci`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `.github/workflows/pr.yml:48` runs `node build/npm/preinstall.ts` immediately before the existing `npm ci`; identical added steps appear in five other changed workflows. The root `package.json:23` already declares that command as the `preinstall` lifecycle script, so `npm ci` invokes it again.
Findings.Title: Avoid running the full preinstall twice on cache misses
Findings.Impact: Cache-miss PR and product-build jobs wait for an extra nested npm installation plus two extra node-gyp header-install subprocesses, increasing pipeline latency, registry/cache I/O, and aggregate CI load across the six newly modified jobs.
Findings.Evidence: `build/npm/preinstall.ts` synchronously runs a nested `npm ci` for `build/npm/gyp`, then invokes `node-gyp install` for both Electron and Node headers and overlays files. The fast-path state lives at `node_modules/.postinstall-state`; these workflow steps run specifically when node_modules restoration missed. Therefore the added explicit call and the existing lifecycle call each launch the nested package installation and header checks/downloads on the build's critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the required early header overlay but avoid rerunning it from the lifecycle: add a focused header-preparation mode/marker and have the subsequent `npm ci` preinstall skip `installHeaders` when that exact preparation has already succeeded, while retaining the version/toolchain checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Node-modules cache-miss installation in the newly changed GitHub and Azure build jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit preinstall must finish before root `npm ci`; root `npm ci` then runs the same preinstall lifecycle before dependency installation can complete, so both executions are serialized on the job's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Twice per cache-miss job after the diff: once from the added step and once from root npm's existing preinstall lifecycle; multiplied across six changed jobs and template/architecture expansions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the root `npm ci` lifecycle launched this nested install, once per successful attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both nested installs must complete before the job can proceed past dependency installation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run node-gyp header installation for Electron and Node distributions, using network when the corresponding node-gyp cache is cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two Electron/Node install checks per full preinstall, and the full preinstall now runs twice per cache-miss job; cold caches can download each distribution while warm caches still incur subprocess and cache checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One full set of header installation calls from the root npm lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous `execFileSync` calls block each preinstall and therefore the dependency-install critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recreate the nested gyp node_modules tree, inspect header caches, and copy custom headers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Repeated by both full preinstall executions on every root node_modules cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Performed once through the npm lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous and serialized before root installation completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of node_modules cache-miss jobs, including architecture/template expansions; effective cardinality is one duplicate full preinstall per such job.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Work is serialized within each job. Independent CI jobs and matrix instances may run concurrently without a shared limiter, increasing aggregate registry/cache and runner I/O load.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A restored root node_modules cache skips both steps. On a miss, the state guard under root `node_modules` is unavailable for both invocations; warm npm/node-gyp caches reduce downloads but do not remove the duplicated nested npm subprocess and filesystem work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: workflow ordering, npm lifecycle registration, synchronous subprocesses, and state-file location are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added seconds depend on npm and node-gyp cache warmth and runner storage/network performance; the duplicated critical-path mechanism and multiplicity are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression; one medium-severity finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux desktop application startup before Electron ready
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new desktop-name selection runs synchronously after userData setup and before code-cache/crash-reporter initialization and app readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous existence check for the fixed installed desktop-file path under `/usr/share/applications`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one stat per non-Snap Linux process startup when `linuxDesktopName` is configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No desktop-file existence check occurred here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks startup briefly, but is a single fixed local metadata lookup with no collection scaling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per Linux application process, independent of workspace, files, windows, or extensions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single call on the main process startup thread; no fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache; normal OS filesystem metadata caching can make warm starts cheaper.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for placement and one-call cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage-specific stat latency varies, but the fixed system path and cardinality keep realistic impact bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded one-time local stat does not establish a meaningful startup regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench and sessions loading local `vscode-file` resources
Scenarios.CriticalPath: HTML, scripts, styles, extension assets, and images request the custom protocol; each allowed resource must be resolved before its consumer can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the corresponding file URL through Electron net.fetch and return its response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One underlying file load per requested resource, with request count controlled by the existing resource graph and renderer cache policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old file-protocol callback returned the same path to Electron, which performed one underlying file load per resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Critical for each resource, including startup HTML/scripts; independent resources are scheduled by Chromium.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and size of requested local application/extension resources; no new per-item fan-out beyond one fetch for each existing request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Chromium/Electron network scheduling controls concurrent resource requests; the diff adds no explicit burst or serial loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Built-resource caching remains governed by Chromium; OSS development cache-control disabling was pre-existing. Cold resources require file reads and warm renderer caches may avoid requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that boundary cardinality remains one per request; low evidence of any regression magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The API migration may have constant wrapper overhead, but repository evidence does not prove an additional file read, lost cache, or materially larger allocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no proven extra boundary, scaling increase, or cache defeat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote HTTP and managed remote-resource loading
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A remote resource request traverses either one HTTP fetch or one main-to-window IPC request and must complete before the resource is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the rewritten HTTP URL using Electron net.fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network fetch per custom-protocol request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old HTTP-protocol registration rewrote to the same HTTP URL and caused one network request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The single fetch remains the resource critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Route one managed resource request to its owning window and receive a base64 response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call per managed resource request, routed to one matching connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old buffer-protocol handler made the same single IPC call and decoded the same base64 body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Response creation waits for the same IPC result as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Decode the base64 body into a Buffer and wrap it in a Response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One decode/buffer per response, unchanged in body-size scaling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The callback path already decoded the body with `Buffer.from(..., 'base64')` once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after IPC and before delivery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and byte size of requested remote resources; effective cardinality remains one network or IPC operation and one decode per request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests remain independently scheduled; no changed loop, limiter, queue, or aggregate fan-out was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: HTTP/Electron caching behavior remains associated with the rewritten fetch; no changed code explicitly disables or expands caches. Managed IPC responses remain uncached in this layer as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from direct before/after handler comparison.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Response-wrapper constants are unmeasured, but expensive boundary count and body-size work are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: protocol API migration preserves expensive-operation cardinality and allocation scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening native save/open dialogs without a caller-provided default URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed methods now await default-path resolution before invoking the existing native-host dialog IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally test existence of configured `files.dialog.defaultPath` when history provides no candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existence check per dialog invocation, only on the preferred-home fallback with a configured path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two generic native-dialog methods forwarded no default path and did not resolve or validate one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly precedes native dialog opening; common history-backed/default-home paths do not perform the exists call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the native host to display the OS save/open dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call per user dialog invocation, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Invoked immediately with no default path when the caller omitted it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still the authoritative dialog boundary; now follows default-path resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user/extension dialog invocation; no collection-dependent work or concurrent fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Default resolution and native IPC are deliberately serialized for one invocation; separate invocations are not newly coalesced or burst-scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: History/configuration reads are in-memory. The optional existence check uses file-provider/OS caching; no new retained cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added await and optional single boundary; uncertain material impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A configured unavailable network path can be slower, but prevalence is narrow and the same resolver is already used by related pick-and-open methods; no broad or collection-scaling regression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded intentional default resolution does not meet the high-confidence performance threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux/Web window-controls-overlay titlebar construction and layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Titlebar creation appends containers once when the part is constructed; CSS environment-variable widths participate in normal titlebar layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional container for Linux WCO titlebars, independent of editor count, rows, frames, or input frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous DOM construction once; no scheduling loop or asynchronous boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from changed constructor and selectors.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible constant DOM/layout cost; no evidence of forced repeated layout or frame-frequency work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: one bounded DOM node and static selectors do not establish rendering regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 39 changed-file patches and traced runtime, build, protocol, dialog, startup, and titlebar paths. Submitted one medium repeated-work finding for duplicated full preinstall execution on cache-miss jobs; no other changed path proved a scaling or critical-path performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
